rules: Before the path starts, pick Life, Life$pan, or Life$pan+. The choice locks when Study or Work begins.
Life is the traditional Game of Life. Squares are events, not years. Paydays stay paydays. A move does not pay or charge expenses on every space. No triangle.

Life$pan: each square is one year. Moving one space pays that year's salary and charges that year's expenses. Former paydays are named Promo?. No triangle. Retirement is named and is not built in this version.

Life$pan+ is the same years, the same per-space pay and expenses, and the same Promo? tile as Life$pan, plus the triangle, both mortality tables, the walker, income, expenses, savings, and 4% interest or borrowing. This replaces the name Entirety. Its two 1-in-10 spins move the triangle and do not change pay.

On Life$pan+, the spinner shows 1 through 10, plus a death wedge. The wedge is this year's death probability, as a fraction of the circle. Landing in it ends the life on the current square. No numbered move.

You resolve the space you land on. Spaces you pass do not fire, except Payday on Life, and except a review on Life$pan and Life$pan+. On Life$pan and Life$pan+, every space you move into still pays that year's salary and charges that year's expenses.
On Life, Payday adds your current salary when you land on it or pass it. Other spaces do not pay salary or charge living expenses.

On Life$pan and Life$pan+, landing on or passing a former payday runs one Promo? outcome from meta.review, then that year pays and charges like any other space. The card shows the odds for the active mode.
A later demotion cannot drop pay below 80% of starting pay. A temporary pay change, and a temporary expense increase, are this year only.
A stop ends the move even if steps remain. Then you spin again.

Ages 18 to 21 are a fork. The choice is Study, or make money right away. Study pays tuition up front and a higher salary after 21. Work skips that debt and starts with cash. That is true on Life, and on Life$pan and Life$pan+. Each path has four spaces, then one shared track from 22 to 68. The house, the cards, the investments, and the kids swing the ending. On Life those squares are not years. On Life$pan and Life$pan+ each square is one year.

At 68 the working track ends. The climb has no downslope. Decumulation is not in this version. On Life$pan+, positive savings earn 4% a year and negative savings pay the 4% borrowing charge. Life and Life$pan do neither. Retirement spaces are not in this version.

One point in the triangle sets health, work, and frugality. Weights are inverse distance to the vertices, so an edge does not freeze the far one. It locks when the path starts. Reviews on Life$pan+ may nudge it later. The center is still one third.

A click on Life, Life$pan, or Life$pan+ starts a new game. Resume loads the name you typed. An empty name does nothing. Every decision uses that same treatment: waiting options vibrate between bold and dim, the picked one stays steady and bold, and the others stay dim. That includes Study or Work, a yes or no, and any other choice. Credit-card debt stacks on every space you move through, and the due square collects the balance even when you only pass it.

College Board, Trends in Student Aid: 2023-24 bachelor's recipients who borrowed left with $29,560 on average. https://research.collegeboard.org/trends/student-aid/highlights
NACE Summer 2026 Salary Survey: Class of 2025 bachelor's average starting salary $67,983. https://www.naceweb.org/job-market/compensation/starting-salaries-climb-for-the-class-of-2025
BLS, employment and wages by typical entry-level education, median annual wage 2025 for high school diploma or equivalent: $48,050. https://www.bls.gov/emp/tables/education-summary.htm

BLS OEWS May 2025: construction trades workers median $58,150; electricians $63,190; electrician helpers about $42,661 ($20.51 an hour). https://www.bls.gov/ooh/construction-and-extraction/electricians.htm

NAR median existing-home price $417,500 in September 2026. 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers: first-time buyer median down payment 10 percent, July 2024 through June 2025. https://www.nar.realtor/press-releases/first-time-home-buyer-share-falls-to-historic-low-of-21-median-age-rises-to-40

FTC Consumer Sentinel 2024: median reported fraud loss $497. More than 120,000 reports lost over $10,000. Stolen identity on this board is an $8,000 hit in that serious range. https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/03/new-ftc-data-show-big-jump-reported-losses-fraud-125-billion-2024

triangle.note: Weights are inverse distance to the vertices. Income and the spending rate still follow axis() against one third. Health-related costs are one quarter of the spending budget. Total annual expenses = income × spend rate × (0.75 + 0.25 × health-cost multiplier). On Life$pan and Life$pan+, each space pays that year's salary and charges that year's full expenses. Life does not. When savings are negative after that, Life$pan+ also charges borrowing at 4% of the amount below zero. When savings are positive, Life$pan+ adds 4% interest for the year. Salary follows the income multiplier.

review.note: Life$pan and Life$pan+ only, when you land on or pass a former payday named Promo?. Life paydays stay paydays. One draw, one outcome. The draw uses its own stream, so the spinner does not move. The two 1-in-10 slots differ by mode. The other five are shared.

spaces.title: Tuition
spaces.detail: Four years of a public in-state budget, due up front. The number is the price, not the average loan.
spaces.adapts: College path opening. Four years of the published public in-state student budget. No gendered campus.

spaces.title: A year
spaces.detail: No bill this year. The card stays closed until you land.
spaces.adapts: Was the study year with no payday. Now a closed flavor year.

spaces.title: Paid internship
spaces.detail: The summer deposit hits the app. Enough for food and a bus pass. Not enough to touch the debt.
spaces.adapts: Late college income, smaller than a career payday.

spaces.title: First role
spaces.detail: You stop. School is over, and the higher pay starts with this job.
spaces.adapts: Job Search stop. Guaranteed, like the classic red space. Higher pay than the work path.

spaces.title: First job
spaces.detail: You make money right away. No tuition. The pay starts today.
spaces.adapts: Career path opening. Immediate job at the high-school-occupation median. No degree gate.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account. The study path does not have this year.
spaces.adapts: Early Payday the career path reaches sooner.

spaces.title: Dead laptop
spaces.detail: The machine you work on dies. The replacement is on you.
spaces.adapts: Early career expense. A dead laptop, in place of a tool kit.

spaces.title: Early raise
spaces.detail: A step toward trade-scale pay, only if you land here. Passing through skips it.
spaces.adapts: From high-school-occupation pay toward the construction-trades median. Land only. Not a stop.

spaces.title: The car
spaces.detail: A used car, the loan, and the insurance. A classic bill, due up front.
spaces.adapts: First household setup after the paths merge.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account.
spaces.adapts: Payday. Collect salary on land or pass.

spaces.title: The lawsuit
spaces.detail: A fender, a lawyer, and a settlement. It comes out of savings.
spaces.adapts: A current mishap. A scam text, settled in cash.

spaces.title: Refund hits
spaces.detail: The tax app drops a refund you did not plan on.
spaces.adapts: Small windfall.

spaces.title: Get married
spaces.detail: You stop. The wedding is the classic one, and the bill is not optional.
spaces.adapts: Get Married stop. No spouse gender, no pink or blue pegs.

spaces.title: Wedding gifts
spaces.detail: A few transfers and one large check. It does not cover the wedding.
spaces.adapts: Honeymoon beat, recast as gifts to the household.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account.
spaces.adapts: Payday. Collect salary on land or pass.

spaces.title: A baby
spaces.detail: You stop. A child joins the house. The crib, the care, and the bills start the day you get home.
spaces.adapts: Baby space. No boy or girl.

spaces.title: Online course
spaces.detail: Nights on a laptop, a fee, and a raise if you finish.
spaces.adapts: Night school. Optional, like a blue space.

choice.prompt: Pay $4,000 for an online course that raises your pay by $4,000?

spaces.title: Credit cards
spaces.detail: The cards arrive and the spending starts. The balance stacks on every space after this one until it comes due.
spaces.adapts: Lost or stolen card. Charges before the freeze. Separate from the lost phone.

spaces.title: A bonus
spaces.detail: A real bonus hits. It is not a second salary.
spaces.adapts: Bonus windfall.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account.
spaces.adapts: Payday. Collect salary on land or pass.

spaces.title: The house
spaces.detail: You stop. The down payment is huge, and it is due before the key. This is the classic house.
spaces.adapts: Buy a House stop. A first-time down payment, not the full sale price and not a deed deck.

spaces.title: Housewarming
spaces.detail: People show up once. A few transfers cover a chair.
spaces.adapts: After the house, a small return.

spaces.title: Twins
spaces.detail: Two more children arrive together. The costs land in one pile.
spaces.adapts: Twins space. No sexes assigned.

spaces.title: A year
spaces.detail: No bill this year. The card stays closed until you land.
spaces.adapts: Breathing room. A flavor card, no cash.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account.
spaces.adapts: Payday. Collect salary on land or pass.

spaces.title: Back taxes
spaces.detail: The letter is not a suggestion. Penalties are already on it.
spaces.adapts: Serious mishap. Stolen online identity. An $8,000 hit.

spaces.title: Promotion
spaces.detail: The new title sticks. Pay moves, if you land here.
spaces.adapts: Midlife raise. Land only.

spaces.title: A year
spaces.detail: No bill this year. The card stays closed until you land.
spaces.adapts: Was a group dinner with a small cost. The cost is zero. A flavor card.

spaces.title: Investing app
spaces.detail: A tip in the app. The odds are on the choice, and they are new each time you land.
spaces.adapts: Stock space. Optional. Fresh odds from 10% through 80%. Win doubles the stake. Otherwise the stake is lost.

choice.prompt: Put $10,000 in? The chance it doubles is on the choice.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account.
spaces.adapts: Payday. Collect salary on land or pass.

spaces.title: An inheritance
spaces.detail: Money from someone who kept their word. It helps. It is not the house.
spaces.adapts: Marketplace sale, in place of selling a painting.

spaces.title: The specialist
spaces.detail: The referral, the scans, and the part insurance will not touch.
spaces.adapts: A stack of subscriptions, in place of a small clinic bill. The later medical year still carries the health cost.

spaces.title: Pay the cards
spaces.detail: You can pay a chunk of the stacked balance now, or let it keep growing.
spaces.adapts: Optional life change, in the spirit of a blue space.

choice.prompt: Pay $70,000 against the card balance now? Otherwise it keeps stacking.
choice.lifePrompt: Pay $50,000 against the card balance now? Otherwise it keeps stacking.

spaces.title: The deductible
spaces.detail: A smaller medical bill, before the hospital. The deductible is yours.
spaces.adapts: Lost phone. The device, separate from the stolen card.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account.
spaces.adapts: Payday. Collect salary on land or pass.

spaces.title: Kid's tuition
spaces.detail: You stop. The child's school bill is yours.
spaces.adapts: Child-related cost without boy/girl framing.

spaces.title: The roof
spaces.detail: The roof goes. Insurance argues. You pay.
spaces.adapts: Was a quiet year. A flavor card, no cash.

spaces.title: Pay bump
spaces.detail: A cost-of-living raise, if this is the year you land.
spaces.adapts: Small raise. Land only.

spaces.title: Side hustle

spaces.adapts: Risky business. Optional. Fresh odds from 10% through 80%. Win doubles the stake. Otherwise the stake is lost.

choice.prompt: Put $10,000 in? The chance it doubles is on the choice.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account.
spaces.adapts: Payday. Collect salary on land or pass.

spaces.title: Cards come due
spaces.detail: You stop. The stacked balance is due in full. Passing through still collects it.
spaces.adapts: Buy now, pay later. A household-scale bill, in place of storm damage.

spaces.title: Recognition
spaces.detail: The work gets seen. Pay moves, if you land here.
spaces.adapts: Late-career raise. Land only.

spaces.title: The operation
spaces.detail: Pay for the operation now, or wait and risk the emergency room.
spaces.adapts: Breathing room. A flavor card, no cash.

choice.prompt: Pay $120,000 for the operation now? Wait, and a 1-in-2 emergency costs $210,000.
choice.lifePrompt: Pay $90,000 for the operation now? Wait, and a 1-in-2 emergency costs $200,000.

spaces.title: Family transfer
spaces.detail: Another transfer arrives. Useful, and not enough to clear a stacked card.
spaces.adapts: Inheritance windfall, gender-neutral.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account.
spaces.adapts: Payday. Collect salary on land or pass.

spaces.title: Support a parent
spaces.detail: A parent needs a year of help. You send it, and it is not small.
spaces.adapts: Family support. No mother/father assignment.

spaces.title: The vacation
spaces.detail: The trip goes on the cards in spirit, and the savings still leave.
spaces.adapts: Was the group tab with a small cost. The cost is zero. A flavor card.

spaces.title: Laid off
spaces.detail: The job ends. The gap between paychecks is on you.
spaces.adapts: Breathing room. A flavor card, no cash.

spaces.title: A windfall
spaces.detail: One invoice clears. A classic lucky square, not a rescue.
spaces.adapts: Late windfall.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account.
spaces.adapts: Payday near the classic early-retirement age. No early retirement choice in this version.

spaces.title: The hospital
spaces.detail: You stop. The procedure is the classic one, and the portal bill is dire.
spaces.adapts: Health cost. Not a death sliver.

spaces.title: The second procedure
spaces.detail: Another medical year. Smaller than the hospital, and still dire.
spaces.adapts: Breathing room. A flavor card, no cash.

spaces.title: A year
spaces.detail: No bill this year. The card stays closed until you land.
spaces.adapts: Was a send-off with a small cost. The cost is zero. A flavor card.

spaces.title: Payday
spaces.detail: Salary hits the account. One year of the track remains.
spaces.adapts: Last Payday before the gate.

spaces.title: Retirement gate
spaces.detail: You stop. Working life ends at 68. This version ends with it.
spaces.adapts: Retire stop. No Millionaire Estates, no annuity, no decumulation.

flavorCards.caption: The cat became a loaf on the warm router.
The dog is wearing one sock and will not explain.
A pigeon took one fry and bowed.
The balloon is still on the mailbox. The party was yesterday.
The goldfish watched the whole film and forgot it.
The little trophy is holding a single sock.
Two eyes in the closet blinked and said excuse me.
Your shadow grew a tail and wagged.
The fridge hummed a lullaby. It was trying to help.
The neighborhood dog led a parade of leaves.
The ball found the net. The bench made a noise.
Your song came on between the cans.
Overtime. The popcorn hit the ceiling.
A bright speck crossed the roof. The chat lost its mind.
The ball left as the buzzer sang.

annuity.name: 2012 IAR
annuity.fullName: 2012 Individual Annuity Reserve Table, calendar year 2026
annuity.role: Reserve table for an individual annuity. Not a pricing table. The 2012 IAM Basic table is the experience table. The 2012 IAM Period table is that basic table with the LATF load, about 10 percent lower qx through age 100. The 2012 IAR is the Period table projected with Scale G2.
annuity.blend: Male and female rates are published separately. q is the 50/50 mean. SOA did not publish that mean.
annuity.youngAges: Published from age 0. Ages 18 through 68 are copied from those columns. No splice.
annuity.sourceNote: Payout Annuity Table Team, 2012 Individual Annuity Reserving Table, September 2011, Exhibit IV. SOA MORT 2585 and 2586 are the male and female 2012 IAM Period tables. MORT 2583 and 2584 are Scale G2. SOA page: https://www.soa.org/resources/experience-studies/2011/2012-ind-annuity-reserving-rpt/ . Checked October 2026: MORT has no 2020, 2024, or 2025 IAM, and the SOA tables page still lists this 2012 reserving table.

life.name: 2017 Loaded CSO
life.fullName: 2017 Loaded CSO Gender-Blended (50% Male) Composite ANB Ultimate
life.role: Statutory valuation table for ordinary life insurance. Loaded, so these qx are the higher public rates. The 2015 VBT underneath is the experience table and is closer to pricing. Pricing practice and the statutory table differ. This series is the statutory one.
life.youngAges: The workbook publishes attained ages 0 through 120. Ages 18 through 68 are the ultimate column. No splice.
life.comparison: 2015 VBT unismoke ANB ultimate rates start at attained age 25. A 50/50 of the published male and female ultimate rates is below this loaded CSO from 25 through 68. At 67 the CSO rate is 11.58 per thousand and that VBT mean is 9.985 per thousand. SOA did not publish the VBT mean. It is not a series in this spec.
